The expert estimated roughly 1-2% of applications (out of the state's annual volume of 50,000-80,000) result in deemed approval, mostly due to portal/technical glitches.

validity.text: Once granted, GST Registration is perpetual with no renewal requirement; only amendment (for changes such as partner/signatory details, HSN code or address) or cancellation (for discontinuation of business) applies thereafter.

fees.text: No registration fee or security deposit is charged. The only monetary requirement is advance tax payment, applicable exclusively to casual taxable persons.

remarks: GST Registration is a standalone, PAN-based, all-India process; it is not linked to or contingent upon approvals from any other department or licence (e.g., Factory Licence, Fire NOC).
The entire process is governed uniformly by the GST Council and implemented through GSTN, with no scope for state-level variation, addition or removal of steps.
The expert noted an inherent policy tension (in their role as EoDB nodal officer) between keeping the process simple and fast for genuine applicants and preventing misuse by fraudulent actors.

findings.text: The GST Registration process is entirely online and paperless, end-to-end, through a single central GST Portal, with no requirement for the applicant to visit any office.
Deemed approval is built into the process: 7 days for Aadhaar-authenticated applications and 30 days for non-Aadhaar-authenticated applications.
A Rule 14A fast-track grants registration within 3 working days for applicants with lower anticipated output tax liability.

Rising use of fake or non-genuine registrations, including cases using stolen identity/Aadhaar details particularly from remote areas, to claim fraudulent input tax credit and refunds, exploiting the simplicity of the process.
Insufficient manpower to detect and act against fake taxpayers was cited as a constraint.
Field verification capacity constraints exist in some jurisdictions — e.g., only two vehicles available for the combined Medinipur-Jharkhand charge — which can delay enforcement.

The expert described an inherent tension between keeping the process simple/fast for genuine applicants and preventing misuse, since universally mandatory physical verification would improve fraud detection but extend the current 7-day timeline.
Strengthen inter-departmental coordination (GST, police, and other enforcement agencies) to curb fake registrations.
Augment manpower and logistics (e.g., vehicles) for field verification and enforcement, particularly in resource-constrained jurisdictions.
Continue to balance Ease-of-Doing-Business objectives against fraud-prevention safeguards, rather than reverting to universally mandatory physical verification.
Sustain and expand outreach and awareness programmes with trade bodies and dealers on procedural changes.
Biometric authentication (fingerprint and iris scan at GST Suvidha Kendras) was introduced as an additional safeguard for non-Aadhaar-authenticated applicants.
Risk flags used by GSTN include the same mobile number/email linked to a previously cancelled or fake dealer, a sudden unexplained turnover spike, and certain fraud-prone sectors.
No registration fee or security deposit is required; the only monetary requirement is advance tax, applicable solely to casual taxable persons.
GST Registration is standalone and not linked to or contingent upon approvals from any other department or licence.

gaps.text: Fully online, paperless registration with built-in deemed approval and a 3-working-day fast-track (Rule 14A) for applicants with lower anticipated tax liability.
Biometric authentication (fingerprint/iris scan at GST Suvidha Kendras) as an additional fraud safeguard for non-Aadhaar-authenticated applicants.
No figure is given for what share of West Bengal's GST registration volume is Aadhaar- versus non-Aadhaar-authenticated.
There is no fixed, publicly defined risk matrix for registration; risk flags rely on 'system-driven flags and officer judgment.'
Suggested strengthening inter-departmental coordination (GST, police, other enforcement bodies) and augmenting field-verification manpower/logistics to curb fake registrations.

timeline.text: GSTR-1 (outward supply details) is due by the 11th of the subsequent month, and GSTR-3B (summary return and tax payment) by the 20th, for regular taxpayers. QRMP taxpayers file GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B quarterly while paying tax monthly; Composition taxpayers pay tax quarterly via CMP-08 and file one annual return (GSTR-4).

licenses.documentsNote: No supporting documents are typically required to be uploaded for routine filing; the taxpayer discloses transaction-wise details electronically. A Digital Signature Certificate is needed for companies (cost noted as approximately Rs. 2,000-3,000 for 3 years); proprietors/individuals can instead authenticate via OTP. Underlying books of account must be maintained but are referenced only if scrutiny or audit is triggered.

deemedApproval.text: Not applicable in the conventional sense — return filing is a self-assessed declaration by the taxpayer rather than an application requiring departmental approval. A demand/assessment arises only where scrutiny identifies a discrepancy, and even then the taxpayer is given an opportunity to respond before any adverse order.

validity.text: Not applicable in the licence/approval sense — tax filing is a recurring periodic compliance obligation (monthly, quarterly, or annual depending on taxpayer category) rather than a one-time approval with a validity period.

fees.text: No fee is charged for filing returns. A late fee of Rs. 100 per day per Act (i.e. Rs. 100 CGST + Rs. 100 SGST = Rs. 200/day) applies for delayed filing, capped at a maximum of Rs. 5,000, and is computed automatically by the portal.

steps.title: Log into GST Portal dashboard
steps.note: Access the return-filing module using login credentials created at registration.

steps.title: File GSTR-1
steps.note: Invoice-wise outward supply details; auto-populates as GSTR-2B (purchase-side input tax credit) for the recipient.

steps.title: File GSTR-3B and pay tax
steps.note: Summary return; tax paid by debiting the electronic cash ledger and/or utilising available input tax credit.

steps.title: Automatic processing
steps.note: Filing and payment are captured and processed automatically; no departmental approval needed for a routine, matched return.

steps.title: Scrutiny on mismatch (if triggered)
steps.note: If a mismatch is detected (e.g., GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B, supplier/recipient, or Income Tax records), the case may be selected for scrutiny, leading to a show cause notice and, if unresolved, an assessment/demand order.

steps.title: Appeal against demand order (if any)
steps.note: Subject to a mandatory pre-deposit of 10% of the disputed tax amount; must be filed within 3 months of the adjudication order, extendable by 1 month for sufficient cause.

ed.location: Not specified in the source recording (session conducted with the State GST Department, West Bengal)

remarks: Tax filing is a distinct process from GST Registration and Refund, though outcomes in filing (e.g., mismatches) can trigger the scrutiny/adjudication route.
There is no requirement for physical verification as part of routine return filing; physical/field involvement arises only through subsequent enforcement or scrutiny action, if triggered.
Scrutiny/audit selections are made periodically; audit selection is stated to be made by the Commissioner annually after database review.

findings.text: Tax filing is fully online, paperless and self-declared; no departmental approval is needed for a routine, matched return.
GSTR-2B (purchase-side input tax credit) auto-populates from the counterparty's GSTR-1, reducing manual reconciliation effort.
Late fees (Rs. 100/day per Act, capped at Rs. 5,000) are computed automatically by the portal.
Differentiated filing frequency (monthly for Regular, quarterly for QRMP and Composition taxpayers) is tailored to taxpayer scale, easing compliance load for smaller businesses.

Mismatches between taxpayer declarations, or against Income Tax data, can trigger scrutiny, notices and eventual assessment/demand, linked by the expert to rising instances of fraudulent input tax credit claims.
Enforcement and scrutiny work is constrained by manpower availability and, in some jurisdictions, limited logistics (e.g., vehicles for field enforcement).
Strengthen data-matching and coordination with other departments (e.g., Income Tax) to identify filing mismatches earlier.
Augment manpower and logistics support for scrutiny, audit and enforcement functions tied to return filing.
Continue simplifying and automating reconciliation while maintaining adequate safeguards against misuse of self-declared filing.
Sustain outreach and awareness programmes with trade bodies and dealers on filing requirements and procedural changes.

An appeal against a demand order requires a mandatory 10% pre-deposit of the disputed tax amount and must be filed within 3 months of the adjudication order, extendable by 1 month for sufficient cause.
A Digital Signature Certificate is required for companies to authenticate filings (noted at approximately Rs. 2,000-3,000 for 3 years); proprietors/individuals can instead use OTP.
Filing itself is not risk-classified, but selection for scrutiny afterward is parameter-driven, based on defined mismatch triggers and departmental intelligence.
Audit selection is made periodically, stated to be by the Commissioner annually after a database review.

gaps.text: Auto-computation of late fees and auto-population of purchase-side input tax credit (GSTR-2B) from the counterparty's GSTR-1.
No specific figure is given for the proportion of filings selected for scrutiny or found to have mismatches.
No quantified threshold is given for what counts as a 'sudden and unexplained spike in turnover' risk flag.
Suggested stronger inter-departmental data-sharing (e.g., with Income Tax) to detect filing mismatches earlier.
Beyond the Medinipur-Jharkhand vehicle example, no overall figures are given for the scrutiny/enforcement manpower or logistics shortfall.

licenses.issuingAuthority: State GST Department, Government of West Bengal (Assistant Commissioner or Deputy Commissioner verifies applications), administered through the GST Portal (GSTN)

timeline.text: Refund must be processed and paid within 60 days of the date of application. If not paid within 60 days, the department is liable to pay the taxpayer interest at 6% per annum for the delay. A refund claim must be filed within 2 years of the relevant transaction (e.g., the export).

documents: Export invoice and consignment/shipping bill (export-related ITC refund)
Sale and purchase documents evidencing the input/output tax-rate differential (inverted duty structure refund)
licenses.documentsNote: No document is required for refund of an excess cash-ledger balance, since this represents the taxpayer's own money. Export-related refund documents are cross-verified against data the exporter has uploaded on the DGFT portal.

deemedApproval.text: No deemed-approval mechanism as such was described for refunds; instead, the process is governed by a mandatory 60-day payment timeline, with the department required to pay 6% annual interest to the taxpayer for any delay beyond that period.

validity.text: Not applicable in the licence/approval sense — refund is a transaction-based claim (tied to a specific export, inverted-duty accumulation, or excess cash balance) rather than an approval with an ongoing validity period.

fees.text: No fee is associated with filing or processing a refund claim, consistent with the broader GST process not levying any application fee.

steps.title: File refund application on GST Portal dashboard
steps.note: Under the relevant category: export-related ITC refund, inverted duty structure refund, or excess cash-ledger balance.

steps.title: Upload and auto-verify export documents
steps.note: For export-related refunds: export invoice and shipping bill, cross-verified against DGFT portal data.

steps.title: Submit sale/purchase documents
steps.note: For inverted duty structure refunds, evidencing the higher input tax rate versus the lower output tax rate.

steps.title: Officer verification
steps.note: Assistant/Deputy Commissioner verifies the application and supporting documentation/data; no document is required for excess cash-ledger-balance refunds.

steps.title: Sanction or show cause notice
steps.note: If the officer is satisfied (and, for exports, DGFT data matches), the refund is sanctioned and credited; if a discrepancy is noticed, a show cause notice may be issued.

steps.title: Processing within statutory timeline
steps.note: Refund processed and paid within 60 days of application; delay beyond 60 days triggers automatic interest payable to the taxpayer.

ed.location: Not specified in the source recording (session conducted with the State GST Department, West Bengal)

remarks: Export-related refunds account for the large majority (around 80%) of refund claims.

Refund claims are not subject to mandatory physical verification; verification, where it occurs, is generally limited to document/data checks (e.g., DGFT matching) rather than site inspection, and site-level checks arise only where there is a specific reason for suspicion or a complaint.

Tax refund is a standalone process, separate from GST Registration, Tax Filing and Adjudication, though a discrepancy identified during refund processing can route the case into scrutiny/adjudication.

findings.text: Tax refund is applied for entirely online through the GST Portal dashboard, with no office visit required.
Export refund claims are automatically cross-verified against DGFT portal data, reducing manual document scrutiny.
No documentation at all is required for refund of an excess cash-ledger balance.
A statutory 60-day processing timeline is backed by mandatory 6% per annum interest payable to the taxpayer for delay.

The rise of fake and non-genuine taxpayers, including cases of stolen identity/Aadhaar details often from remote areas, exploiting the process to claim fraudulent ITC and refunds, was flagged as the single biggest pain point from the administrative side.
Insufficient manpower to detect and act against fake taxpayers claiming fraudulent refunds was cited as a constraint.

Field/enforcement capacity constraints in some jurisdictions (e.g., limited vehicles for the combined Medinipur-Jharkhand charge) can affect the department's ability to act within statutory timelines.
Strengthen inter-departmental coordination (GST, police and other enforcement bodies) to identify and act against fraudulent refund/ITC claims linked to fake taxpayers.
Augment manpower and logistics for verification and enforcement, particularly in resource-constrained jurisdictions, to help meet the 60-day refund timeline consistently.
Continue to balance the ease and speed of the refund process against fraud safeguards, rather than defaulting to universally mandatory physical verification.
Continue leveraging automated data-matching (e.g., with DGFT) as a model for reducing manual verification burden while maintaining fraud control.
A parameter-driven risk approach applies system-wide (registration, filing and refund alike), with history of association with a fake dealer described as the principal risk driver.
A refund claim must be filed within 2 years of the relevant transaction, such as the export.

The expert estimated that mandatory physical verification could eliminate an estimated 80-90% of refund-related fraud but would trade off against the speed and simplicity that make the current process taxpayer-friendly.

gaps.text: Statutory 60-day processing timeline backed by mandatory 6% annual interest for delay, and automated DGFT cross-verification for export refunds.
No documentation required for refund of an excess cash-ledger balance.
No figure is given for the average actual refund processing time against the 60-day statutory cap.
There is no fixed, publicly defined risk matrix for refund-claim scrutiny beyond 'system-driven flags and officer judgment.'
Suggested strengthened inter-departmental coordination and augmented manpower/logistics to curb fraudulent claims while preserving refund speed.

licenses.issuingAuthority: Urban Local Body (ULB) Water Department, under the Urban Development & Municipal Affairs (UD&MA) Department, Government of West Bengal

timeline.text: The expert indicated a timeline of 15 working days for the water connection. Delays were reported mainly for building plan approval, which delays the Occupancy Certificate and therefore the water connection that depends on it.

documents: Plumber's certificate / water supply layout drawing
licenses.documentsNote: Property-tax and land documents are additionally checked by the Dealing Assistant. A standalone water connection application cannot be filed without an OC — the OC must be obtained first if not already held.

deemedApproval.text: No deemed approval exists for water connection or for building plan approval; the expert said there is no option for it under the current rules.

validity.text: There is no single statewide validity period specified for all water connections. The applicable validity depends on the type of connection and the authority providing it, such as a municipality, development authority, or the Irrigation & Waterways/Water Resources Investigation Department.

fees.text: The fee is calculated automatically by the portal; the discussion does not give a clear fee structure for water connection.

steps.title: Log in to the single-window portal
steps.note: SWS "Abhipas"/e-Griho Naksha portal, where water connection and other services are available.

steps.title: Occupancy Certificate check
steps.note: Applicant is asked whether an OC is held; if not, a standalone water connection application cannot be filed and the OC must be obtained first.

steps.title: Upload OC and plumber's certificate
steps.note: Water supply layout drawing uploaded, confirming the line drawing is accurate.

steps.title: Routing to ULB Dealing Assistant and Water Department
steps.note: Dealing Assistant checks property tax/legal documents; Water Department scrutinises the water supply plan.

steps.title: Automatic fee calculation and online payment
Water Department approval
steps.note: If water is unavailable in the area, applicant receives a Non-Availability of Water certificate instead of rejection; for any other rejection, reasons must be stated and the applicant restarts the process.

ed.location: District Industry Centre, Kolkata, 11A&B, Esplanade East, Kolkata -69
ed.designation: Additional Chief Engineer, MED; Project Coordinator, OBPAS-VDMA, Tetra Int

remarks: Water connection and sewer/drainage connection have been integrated with the OC application, so an applicant can request them together with the OC, or apply for them later in standalone mode; the sewer/drainage workflow is similar to the water connection workflow.
Applicants need empanelled consultants for the technical part of building plan applications, with no departmental mandate on the consultant's fee.
The department runs awareness sessions and a master-trainer model for ULB staff.

findings.text: The process is fully online through a single-window portal; applicants do not need to visit the department, though a physical help desk is available for those who do.
A standalone water connection cannot be applied for without an Occupancy Certificate, creating a structural dependency on the building plan approval/OC process.
Delays in building plan approval and the OC cascade into delays for the water connection that depends on them.
The main burden is delay due to manpower shortage in ULBs, where much of the staff is contractual; this was the main complaint received from applicants.
NOC-integrated departments follow their own timelines instead of the 15-day mandate, indirectly affecting water connection via building plan approval.
Holding municipal building committee meetings is difficult, which affects building plan approval and indirectly reaches water connection.
Payment gateway downtime halts progress at the payment step.
The system generates a Non-Availability of Water certificate, rather than a bare rejection, where water is not available in the area.
A grievance redressal system is built into the portal; the department also offers a physical help desk, dedicated email and phone support.
The fee is calculated automatically by the system.
Add a second payment gateway so applications are not held up when one gateway is down.
Issue a central government mandate that all integrated departments follow the 15-day timeline, with state-level rules amended to match.
Increase manpower in ULBs.
Upgrade portal infrastructure and give orientation training to new consultants and ULB staff on building-plan-related services.
The expert said payments applicants make are purely for regulatory compliance and no extra charges are levied.
The Water Department has its own inspection/approval checklist, and no common checklist exists across departments involved in building-related services.

gaps.text: No clear fee structure is given for water connection; the discussion states only that the fee is calculated automatically by the portal.
Validity period of water connections is not standardised statewide — it depends on the type of connection and the providing authority.
A Non-Availability of Water certificate is issued, instead of a bare rejection, when water is unavailable in the area, giving applicants a clear status rather than an ambiguous refusal.
Suggested a central government mandate making the 15-day timeline binding on NOC-integrated departments, alongside matching state-rule amendments.
The exact share of ULB staff that is contractual — cited as driving the manpower shortage — is not quantified.
